newsitem.title: INDIA: Election for Mother Teresa's successor delayed.
newsitem.headline: Election for Mother Teresa's successor delayed.

text.p: The election to choose a successor to Mother Teresa at the head of the Missionaries of Charity religious order has been postponed from February 2, the office of Archbishop of Calcutta Henry D'Souza said on Tuesday.
The archbishop's office gave no explanation for the postponement and did not set a new date for the election. It said the ailing 86-year-old Roman Catholic nun had agreed to the postponement.

More than 100 nuns began a two-week retreat on January 16 to select a successor to the 1979 Nobel Peace Prize winner, who has been taken to hospital three times since August, twice for heart trouble and once after hitting her head in a fall.
"The election of the Superior General of the Missionaries of Charity Sisters will not be held on February 2, 1997, as previously foreseen," the archbishop's secretariat said.

"The General Chapter will enter into the deliberations first," it said, referring to the 103-member electoral college formed to name a successor to the order's founder. "Mother Teresa has given her consent to this request."

The nuns had been scheduled to vote by secret ballot for a successor to Mother Teresa, who in the last vote in 1990 was persuaded to stay on as head of the order she formed in 1948 in India's most densely populated city.
